meta.title: Published annual-average grid emissions intensity by province
meta.basis: ECCC/NIR electric-utility emissions over electric-utility generation

sources.ghg_numerator: StatCan 38-10-0097, sector 'Electric power generation, transmission and distribution [BS22110]' (ECCC NIR data), kt CO2e
sources.generation_denominator: StatCan 25-10-0015, class 'Electricity producers, electric utilities', annual sum, MWh

meta.national_validation: Canada computes to ~101 g/kWh (2022) vs ECCC's published headline 100 g/kWh.
meta.scope_caveats: ON runs ~10-20% below TAF's Annual AEF (TAF attributes all grid emissions to gas). AB runs ~20% below Alberta.ca Fig.7 (cogeneration emission allocation). These are scope differences, documented in METHODOLOGY.md, not errors. This annual basis is DISTINCT from the tool's hourly EF surface.

nl.marginal_note: Hydro-dominant (Churchill Falls / Muskrat Falls). Marginal set equal to the annual average; thermal (Holyrood) or import margin unmodeled.

pe.marginal_note: Mostly wind plus imports from New Brunswick over the Northumberland cables; effective marginal tracks the NB import. Marginal set equal to the annual average as a screening placeholder.

ns.marginal_note: Nova Scotia's grid still leans on coal/petcoke; the marginal unit for new winter load is usually a thermal (coal or gas) plant.

nb.marginal_note: New Brunswick's mixed fleet (nuclear/hydro/coal/oil/gas) meets incremental winter load mostly from gas/oil thermal units.

qc.marginal_note: This province has an hourly marginal surface (ef_surface_qc.json); use that for a real marginal basis. The ECCC yearly-average value here is average-basis only.

on.marginal_note: This province has an hourly marginal surface (ef_surface_on.json); use that for a real marginal basis. The ECCC yearly-average value here is average-basis only.

mb.marginal_note: Hydro-dominant (Manitoba Hydro). Domestic margin is hydro (near-zero); winter-import margin higher but unmodeled. Marginal set equal to the annual average, with this caveat.

sk.marginal_note: SaskPower fleet is coal- and gas-heavy; coal or gas CCGT is typically the marginal unit serving new winter load.

ab.marginal_note: This province has an hourly marginal surface (ef_surface_ab.json); use that for a real marginal basis. The ECCC yearly-average value here is average-basis only.

bc.marginal_note: Hydro-dominant. Domestic margin is flexible hydro (near-zero), but incremental winter demand is frequently served by imports or gas (FortisBC/US). Import-margin intensity is contested and unmodeled -- marginal is set equal to the annual average here, with this caveat (same treatment as Quebec in the hourly pipeline).
